chapter_note: This chapter is largely a systematic cosmological list of the Twelve Judges (a numbered emanational schema) with brief narrative functions for each—typical of the older correspondential-teaching layer. A late drift appears at the end: an explicit hortatory application to the audience (¶16), and an institutional intrusion (“holy church”) within the otherwise cosmic description of the Light Mind (¶13).

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogic frame (“Once again… disciples”), characteristic of the editorial/hagiographic wrapper.

paragraphs.core_text: Twelve judges exist; the great mighty givers of judgement! They were sent and came from the exalted greatness to this place. They were assigned to different works according to the command that the Judge, who belongs to the greatness, entrusted to all these judges. Now he, the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges, who exists and is established in the aeons of greatness; he is the Father of Greatness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological exposition establishing a numbered structure (twelve) and the transcendent Judge (Father of Greatness); no citation, no institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: The first judge is the First Man, he who humiliated the ruler of Darkness in the beginning. He judged him according to a judgement of righteousness; for he had exalted himself against a kingdom that was not his own.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-historical function of a named emanation (First Man) within the Light–Darkness conflict; internal-to-cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: The second judge is the Living Spirit, he who came and bore up the Man. He too made a judgement on all the powers of Darkness; which had wounded the garments of the First Man.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic continuation of the numbered list; cosmological agents and actions, no audience address.

paragraphs.core_text: The third judge is the Mother of Life, the Great Spirit, she who beautified and set up the heavenly part of the universe, according to her pleasure; which [...] her. She judged the rulers above; she fettered and set them firmly in the place that is fitting for them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic construction/ordering language (setting up the universe; fettering rulers) typical of the older teaching substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: The fourth judge is the Great Builder, he who built the new aeon of joy. He judged, according to a judgement of righteousness, the storehouses of the Enemy; that death may not well up from this time on. He has constructed a prison for the Enemy. Also, upon the crown of the building he has constructed a throne for the First Man and all the fathers of light; they who engaged the struggle with the Evil One and were victorious over him.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological mechanics (new aeon, prison, throne) and emanational actors; teleological clause remains within cosmic process (not moral exhortation).

paragraphs.core_text: The fifth judge is the great King of Honour, he who dwells and is established in the seventh firmament. He is the judge of all the firmaments who gives a true judgement, according to a judgement of righteousness, upon all the powers and all the kingdoms of the firmaments.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Degree-structured cosmic geography (seventh firmament) and systematic judging function; no institutional referents.

paragraphs.core_text: The sixth judge is [the Th]ird Ambassador, he who came and displayed his image. He purified the light [...] which his own [...] also of the enemy, he has [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Named cosmological being (Third Ambassador) with image-display/purification function; lacunae do not obscure its systematic placement in the list.

paragraphs.core_text: The seventh judge is ... ... the worlds [... as he gives the victory to] they who are steadfast; but he condemns the ones who are convicted ... ... he shall become for them the steps of the way (?) [...]; but the convicted he sweeps and casts out to the depths.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite heavy lacunae, the voice remains functional/cosmological (victory/condemnation; casting to depths) rather than direct exhortation to the audience.

paragraphs.core_text: The eighth judge is Jesus the Splendour; because after the Ambassador had displayed his image and the light was taken [...] a mass of rulers rose up from above and below. Then they sent Jesus the Splendour. He came ... ... he descended and made a judgement in the firmaments. He separated the steadfast from the convicted.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the ecclesial/Christianizing epithet “the father of all the apostles;” as a later identification reaching into post-cosmic institutional terminology (“apostles”) rather than describing Jesus the Splendour’s cosmic function.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core is the cosmological dispatch and judging action of Jesus the Splendour in the firmaments. The phrase about “apostles” signals a later community’s institutional vocabulary grafted onto a cosmic name.

paragraphs.core_text: The ninth judge is the Virgin of Light, [she who took the heart] of the powers by her image, gathering her own ones into her. She makes a judgement on the ruler of the moist, and the ruler of the dry.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Correspondential-cosmological language (“image,” rulers of moist/dry) and systematic list continuation; entirely within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: The tenth judge is the Judge who dwells in the atmosphere, judging all mankind. He makes a separation between they who are good and they who are evil, setting apart the righteous from the sinners.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological separation is stated as the function of a cosmic Judge “in the atmosphere.” Moral terms appear, but they operate as categories in a cosmic sorting mechanism rather than exhortation to the audience.

paragraphs.core_text: The eleventh judge is the Light Mind, he who shall come and appear in the world. And he unveils [...] and separates light from Darkness, and sets the truth apart from lawlessness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional clause “And he chooses the holy church,” as a cosmos→institution identification (editorial present) inserted into an otherwise cosmic description of the Light Mind’s separating action.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Light Mind as an eschatological cosmic agent fits the numbered emanational schema; “holy church” is an institutional referent that crosses the boundary from BEING (cosmos) to POINTING AT (community structure).

paragraphs.core_text: The twelfth judge is the great counsel, which is the summons and the obedience, which is appointed in the elements. It is the one that makes a separation between the good and the evil ones. At the end also it can gather itself together and sculpt its own self in the Last Statue. And it separates light from darkness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Abstract-but-systematic cosmic hypostasis (“great counsel” appointed in the elements) with eschatological transformation (“Last Statue”); internal cosmological mechanics.

paragraphs.core_text: These are the twelve great and mighty judges who were sent. They came from the great Judge, he who transcends all the judges. He is the Father that is hidden and immeasurable, the one who exists; who is established in the aeons of greatness upon the great throne of honour, which is the King of Honour [...] in his kingdom.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Formal recapitulation closing the cosmic list by returning to the transcendent Father; no exhortation/citation.

Direct audience address and imperatives (“my beloved ones… you yourselves may walk… Judge… May a brother…”) with practical soteriological application—classic late pastoral/application layer, consistent with the chapter’s second-half drift.
